clue.text: Transport sandwiches round centre of Timbuktu

indicators.note: the sandwiches go round, i.e. enclose, the next piece

parts.note: double-deckers are sandwiches made with three slices of bread and two layers of filling

indicators.note: the middle two letters of the eight-letter name Timbuktu are taken

explanation.surface: Some form of transport carries snacks around the heart of a remote African town.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-decker bus is a two-storey vehicle used for public transport.

clue.text: Speaker in parliament perhaps berated if stumbling

indicators.note: stumbling words come out jumbled, so the letters of berated are rearranged

explanation.surface: A member speaking in the House gets told off if they trip over their words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks in a formal debate, as an MP in parliament does, is a debater; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Where students are working? Yes and no

definitions.text: Where students are working? Yes and no

parts.words: Where students are working? Yes and no
parts.note: split into a university plus a word for 'working' it says where students are busy; yet the students' club building is where they go to relax, hence 'yes and no'

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether students actually do any work.
explanation.walkthrough: UNI (university) + ON (working) describes students at work, yes; but the students' union is the bar and social centre, so no.
explanation.definitionFit: A students' union is the club and building where students gather, and the word splits into a place of study plus 'working'.

clue.text: Horrid look given by son during party

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: the son comes during, i.e. inside, the party

parts.note: an at-home is a party held in one's own house

explanation.surface: A son pulls a nasty face at a family gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome and horrid are synonyms, both meaning detestable or repulsive.

clue.text: Unload small amount of alcohol

definitions.meaning: to unload a cargo is to ... it off
a ... is a small measure of drink, as in 'a ... of whisky'

explanation.definitionFit: To drop goods is to unload them, and a drop is also a tiny tot of spirits.

clue.text: Wrongdoer heard pub offered mineral

indicators.note: signals that the word for wrongdoer is said aloud, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A sinner overheard being served at a pub is offered a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is a red mineral, mercury sulphide, the main ore of mercury.

clue.text: Object you reportedly supply

indicators.note: signals a sound-alike: the phrase end you said aloud gives a word of the same sound

parts.note: an end is an object or aim, as in 'to that end', followed by the word you

explanation.surface: Someone tells you what they are objecting to, they say.
explanation.walkthrough: END (object, aim) + YOU, said aloud as one word, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or provide someone with a quality, so it means supply.

clue.text: Punishment? Thrashing's no good, leading to trouble

indicators.note: means the letter for good is removed from the word

parts.note: basting is an old word for a thrashing or beating
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A grim reflection that flogging does no good and only leads to more trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from BASTING to leave BASTIN, and 'leading to' joins it to ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: The bastinado is a punishment of beating the soles of the feet with a stick.

clue.text: Succeeded, having recorded hit

parts.note: s. is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies and lists of rulers
to log something is to record it

explanation.surface: Someone did well, having got a recorded hit to their name.
explanation.definitionFit: To slog a ball is to hit it hard, so slogged means hit, especially in cricket.

clue.text: Musical entertainment broadcast on GB radio

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A stage show is put out on British radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigadoon is a Lerner and Loewe stage musical about a Scottish village that appears once a century.

clue.text: Dance music is included in old recording that needs turning over

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the turned-around letters
the old recording is turned over, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a CD is a recording

explanation.surface: Some music is on a vintage record that needs flipping to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old recording' suggests vinyl, but here it is two pieces turned round to give DCO; 'that needs' is only linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is the style of dance music popular in the 1970s.

clue.text: Small portions of wine harmless? Extremely

parts.note: tent is a deep-red Spanish wine, used for communion

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of harmless are taken

explanation.surface: A drinker asks whether a little wine does any harm and is told it does, at the extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth is a small portion, one of ten equal parts of a whole.

clue.text: Carry out best man's duty, dithering

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the best man's job at a wedding is to have the ring ready
a Scottish and northern word for dithering or vacillating

explanation.definitionFit: Havering means hesitating, and read as 'have ring' it is the best man's wedding task.

clue.text: Preacher Man, first of tracks in album finally released

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the shortened record
the final letter of the word for album is let go

parts.note: an album is a record

indicators.note: the first letter of tracks is taken

explanation.surface: The song Son of a Preacher Man opens an album finally put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally released' drops the last letter of RECORD to leave RECOR, and T goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest, a churchman who preaches.

clue.text: One of several characters in agreement

definitions.meaning: letters like b, c and d are characters of the alphabet that are not vowels

explanation.definitionFit: A consonant is a non-vowel letter, and as an adjective it means harmonious or in agreement.

clue.text: Coarse, loud men by side of a road

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
an army is a body of men

explanation.surface: Rough, noisy soldiers are camped at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmyard as an adjective describes earthy, crude humour or behaviour, so it means coarse.

clue.text: It's time to replace lines in very dry sherry: get shrub

indicators.note: the time letter is to replace, i.e. take the place of, the lines letters
the swap happens in, i.e. inside, the name of the sherry

parts.note: manzanilla is a very dry pale sherry from Andalusia

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap lines in a dry sherry to produce a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' and 'in' together: T replaces LL in MANZANILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Manzanita is an evergreen shrub of the American West with smooth red bark.

clue.text: Arrest me, waving flag

indicators.note: moving to and fro, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A protester waving a banner dares the police to arrest them.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant.

clue.text: Check by soldiers about to stop feud

indicators.note: the word for check goes about, i.e. around, the word for stop

parts.note: to vet is to check
to end is to stop
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve of soldiers

explanation.surface: An inspection by troops is about to put an end to a long quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter feud, especially between families.

clue.text: Trace GI Steve, involved in manoeuvres

indicators.note: being put through manoeuvres rearranges the letters of the soldier's name

explanation.surface: An American soldier called Steve takes part in military exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a trace or remnant of something that has mostly gone.

clue.text: Canon is tiddly after a port

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the letter a
tiddly means slightly drunk, so the word canon staggers into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchman is tipsy after a visit to the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancona is a port city on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Fellow worker given sweet substance, lacking energy

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect in crosswords

indicators.note: the word for the sweet substance goes without the energy letter

parts.note: honey is a sweet substance
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A worker is given something sweet but has no energy left.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony is a man's name, and a fellow is a man.

clue.text: Enrolled in Nazi organisation disreputable incompetents

indicators.note: the word for disreputable is enrolled, i.e. put inside, the organisation

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation
louche means disreputable or of dubious character

explanation.surface: Shady losers signed up to a sinister Nazi body.
explanation.definitionFit: A slouch is an incompetent or lazy person, as in 'no slouch'.

clue.text: Country at centre of plot

indicators.note: only a central stretch of the word for plot is kept, its ends trimmed away

parts.note: a machination is a crafty plot

explanation.surface: A nation sits at the heart of a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at centre of' trims MA from the front and TION from the back of MACHINATION.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a country in East Asia.

clue.text: Seal half-chewed, swallowed by carnivore

indicators.note: the half-word goes inside the carnivore

parts.note: a cat is a meat-eating animal

indicators.note: the first half of the letters of chewed is taken

explanation.surface: A seal half eaten by a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' tempts as the animal for a carnivore to eat, but it is the definition, in its sense of a stamp or mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachet is a seal, originally one on a letter, now also a mark of prestige.

clue.text: Non-British custom on island, one in the Caribbean

indicators.note: means the British letter is taken away

parts.note: a habit is a custom

explanation.surface: A custom that is not British is found on an island in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non' removes B from HABIT, leaving HAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a country on the island of Hispaniola, one of the Caribbean nations.

clue.text: Fruit gobbled up by frail guy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the answer is swallowed inside the words frail guy
the answer is swallowed inside the words frail guy

explanation.surface: A thin man eats some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, frail guy contains UGLI.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: I damage one type of exotic porcelain

parts.note: to mar is to damage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to breaking a piece of foreign china.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is a type of Japanese porcelain, decorated in red, blue and gold.

clue.text: VIP making endless stink among company of wise men

indicators.note: the shortened stink goes among the wise men

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for stink is cut off

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: An important figure makes a bad smell among the Three Wise Men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company of wise men' reads as one phrase, but company and wise men are separate pieces; niff is everyday British slang for a pong.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifico is a grandee or important person, originally a Venetian magnate.

clue.text: More foreign currency I obtained in airport abroad, surprisingly

parts.note: extra means more

indicators.note: the currency and I are obtained in, i.e. placed inside, the airport

parts.note: Orly is an airport in Paris
the dinar is the currency of several countries such as Serbia and Tunisia

explanation.surface: A traveller is amazed to get extra cash changed at a foreign airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraordinarily means remarkably or surprisingly.
